title: Security & Compliance: RBAC, Audit Logging, Data Residency, Retention, Secure SDLC, Incident Response & Evidence Workflows
author: Asha Patel
summary: Comprehensive, operational guidance for Redwood Inference security and compliance controls covering role-based access control (RBAC) and authentication, audit logging requirements, data residency and retention policies, Secure SDLC checkpoints, incident response security requirements, compliance evidence collection workflows, and the risk & exceptions process.

4. Audit Logging

scope: This document applies to all Redwood Inference services (hosted API, Dedicated, Private), supporting infrastructure, developer and operator tooling, and third-party services that process or store customer data. It is required reading for engineering, SRE, security, product, and ops teams responsible for service design, deployment, and compliance evidence delivery.
responsibilities:
- Security team: policy definition, periodic review, audit evidence curator, approval authority for risk exceptions.
- Engineering teams: implement RBAC, authentication, and audit hooks per standards; keep instrumentation and telemetry enabled.
- Eng-SRE: maintain centralized logging, retention pipelines, and monitoring for audit log integrity.
- Product & Legal: provide policy interpretation for customers and respond to data residency requests.
- Compliance: collect and maintain artifacts for assessments (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).
rbac_and_auth_intro: Objectives: least-privilege enforcement, separation of duties, multi-factor authentication for interactive access, and machine identity best practices for services and CI/CD.
rbac_and_auth_controls:
- Authorization model: attribute-based RBAC layered on Vault-managed groups; roles map to least-privilege collections of permissions.
- Identity providers (IdP): OIDC with SCIM provisioning for GSuite and Okta; SAML support for enterprise customers in Private.
- MFA: mandatory for all human accounts with console or admin privileges; recommended for all employees.
- Service identities: short-lived certificates (SPIFFE) or Vault-issued tokens; no long-lived static secrets in repo.
- Privileged access: Just-in-time (JIT) elevation via PAM for sensitive operations; approval logs stored in audit service.
- Access review cadence: quarterly owner-led reviews for all high-privilege roles; automated reminders to role owners.
- Key rotation: rotate all signing keys and Vault root tokens every 90 days; rotate service account credentials on a 30/90 day schedule depending on sensitivity.
rbac_matrix_table:
| Role | Typical Owners | Access Scope | Approval Required | Review Frequency |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| infra-admin | Platform eng | Full cloud account (no billing) | VP platform | Quarterly |
| runtime-operator | Serving runtime team | Deploy/scale/runtime configs | Team lead | Quarterly |
| support-analyst | Customer success | Read-only customer configs, redact PII | Manager | Bi-annually |
| security-auditor | Security | Read-only audit/logs/alerts | CISO | Quarterly |
auth_flow_and_examples:
Example: Service-to-service auth using SPIFFE + Vault.
- 1) Workload mints SVID from SPIFFE agent.
- 2) Workload exchanges SVID for short-lived Vault token via authentication backend.
- 3) Token used to fetch secrets; token TTL <= 1 hour.
CLI example (human MFA + JIT):
- redwood auth login --idp okta --mfa
- redwood elevate --role infra-admin --duration 1h --approval-ticket INC-1234
audit_logging_intro: Goals: provide immutable, auditable evidence of access, configuration changes, data flows, and security-relevant events to support forensic investigations and compliance attestations.
audit_logging_requirements:
- Events to capture: auth successes/failures, token issuance/rotation, role elevation, configuration changes (deployments, infra changes), data exports, admin console actions, customer data access, and retention policy modifications.
- Log format: structured JSON (timestamp, principal, principal_type, action, resource, resource_id, outcome, request_id, trace_id, metadata).
- Delivery: all audit events MUST be forwarded to the central audit cluster (immutable storage) and indexed in the security SIEM.
- Tamper-evidence: compute and store event checksums with daily signed manifests.
- Retention and archival: see Data Residency & Retention section.
- Access control: audit logs are only viewable by security-auditor, eng-sre, and authorized compliance roles. Access requests must be filed when cross-team access is needed.
audit_logging_integrity_playbook:
1) Incident: suspected tampering or missing logs.
2) Verification: compare SIEM index counts vs audit cluster manifests for the timeframe.
3) Forensic snapshot: take immutable snapshot of audit store.
4) Escalation: notify CISO and legal; open a security incident ticket.
5) Remediation: restore missing ingestion pipelines, replay retained raw events where available, and patch instrumentation.
6) Post-incident: update runbooks and update evidence for auditors.
data_residency_and_retention_intro: Policy objective: meet contractual commitments for data locality and retention while minimizing risk and operational complexity.
data_residency_principles:
- Data residency zones: US, EMEA, APAC. Customers can select residency for stored customer data (e.g., embeddings, customer files).
- Control plane vs data plane: control plane metadata may be stored region-aggregate in the primary region (US); customer data plane storage honors residency selection for persistent stores and backups.
- Cross-border transfers: allowed only when covered by contract clause or approved SCCs/Standard Contractual Clauses. Data transfers are logged and require DPO approval.
- Private deployments: customers specifying on-prem or VPC keep full data locality guarantees and are subject to separate SOWs.
- Encryption at rest and in transit always enabled (AES-256 at rest, TLS1.2+ in transit).
retention_policies_table:
| Data Category | Retention Default | Backup Retention | Justification/Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Audit logs (security) | 7 years | 7 years (immutable archive) | Compliance (SOC2/ISO) requirement |
| Customer embeddings | 90 days default | 365 days optional (customer opt-in) | Cost/utility tradeoff; customer-managed option for Private |
| Short-term request logs (LLM requests) | 30 days | 90 days (if needed for debugging) | Minimize PII exposure; redaction applied |
| Billing/usage | 7 years | 7 years | Financial and contractual requirement |
data_deletion_and_customer_requests:
- Data deletion flow: customer submits deletion request -> Support case created -> Orchestration job invoked to delete indexes/blobs and redact logs -> Verification report generated and stored as evidence.
- SLA: standard deletion requests completed within 30 days; expedited within 5 business days for high-priority cases.
- Proof of deletion: sha256 manifests of remaining index manifests and deletion job logs retained in compliance evidence store (access-controlled).
secure_sdlc_overview: Secure SDLC checkpoints are embedded into the product lifecycle: design, implementation, review, pre-release, and post-release monitoring. The goal is to reduce vulnerabilities by design and ensure evidence for audits.
secure_sdlc_checkpoints:
1) Design: threat model completed and approved for any feature touching customer data or auth flows.
2) Implementation: use static analysis (SAST) and dependency vulnerability scans; high severity findings MUST be remediated before merge.
3) Review: security code review conducted for privileged paths, crypto, and auth code.
4) Pre-release: run DAST against staging with production-like data (sanitized); run privacy-preserving fuzz tests for input handling.
5) Release: feature toggles and canary rollout with rollback criteria defined.
6) Post-release: telemetry and alerting tuned; run automated regression tests for security-sensitive flows.
Checklist (developers must attach to PR): threat-model-id, SAST report link, dependency-scan link, security-reviewer sign-off, rollout-plan, and rollback-plan.
sdlc_tooling_and_commands:
- CI gates: pipeline checks include 'snyk test', 'gosec' (or equivalent), and 'checkov' for infra IaC.
- Example CI step snippet:
  - name: Run SAST
    run: snyk test --file=go.mod --severity-threshold=high
- Secrets policy: pre-commit hooks run 'git-secrets' and 'trufflehog' scanning; any commit containing secrets will fail CI.
incident_response_security_intro: Security incident response integrates with company-wide incident processes but has additional evidence preservation and forensics requirements.
incident_response_security_steps:
1) Identification: Security or SRE detects anomalous behavior or receives external report.
2) Triage: classify impact vector (data exfiltration, service compromise, misconfiguration).
3) Evidence preservation: snapshot affected VMs/containers, preserve audit logs, and capture network flows into immutable storage.
4) Containment: apply ACLs, revoke compromised credentials, rotate keys, execute playbook steps (see runbooks).
5) Eradication: remove malware/backdoors, patch vulnerabilities, and validate baseline.
6) Recovery: staged restore to production with monitoring and canary verification.
7) Post-incident: write a postmortem with root cause analysis, timeline, affected customers, regulatory notifications, and action items.
- Notifications: legal and CISO must be notified within 24 hours for incidents classified as PII exposure or regulatory impact.
- Forensics SLA: initial evidence snapshot within 4 hours of incident assignment during business hours.
forensics_and_chain_of_custody:
- Maintain Chain-of-Custody (CoC) metadata for all preserved artifacts (collector, timestamp, SHA256, storage location, access log).
- Use immutable storage with signed manifests for forensic evidence.
- Limit access to evidence to security and legal; any forensic access is logged as an audit event.
compliance_evidence_workflows_intro: Objective: provide repeatable, auditable collections of artifacts that support internal and external assessments (SOC2, ISO27001, customer audits).
compliance_evidence_workflows_steps:
1) Evidence catalog: security maintains a catalog of required artifacts by control (policies, runbooks, SSO/SAML configs, key rotation logs).
2) Automated collection: pipelines export evidence (S3 snapshots, IAM policy exports, audit log manifests) to the Evidence Vault.
3) Review and enrich: security reviewers attach contextual notes and approvals.
4) Evidence packaging: produce a time-bound evidence package for auditors with integrity checksums and signed manifests.
5) Deliverable: provide audit package via secure share (time-limited) or upload to customer portal.
6) Retention: evidence packages retained per retention policy.
evidence_automation_examples:
- Scripted example to export IAM policies: curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://api.redwood.internal/v1/iam/export > iam-policy-$(date +%F).json
- Scheduled job: daily evidence snapshot (00:00 UTC) produces signed manifest and pushes archived package to long-term archive.
- Evidence access: requests must include justification and expiration date; access is reviewed and approved by Security.
risk_and_exceptions_intro: When a standard control cannot be implemented (technical constraints, customer requirement, third-party limitation), teams must file a formal risk exception request. Exceptions are time-boxed and include compensating controls.
risk_and_exceptions_process:
1) Submit request: use the Risk Exception template in Governance tracker with rationale, impacted systems, compensating controls, and proposed mitigation timeline.
2) Review: Security assesses risk severity and recommends approval/denial; High-risk requests escalate to CISO and CTO.
3) Approval: approved exceptions receive an owner, expiration date, and monitoring requirements.
4) Monitoring: owner must provide monthly status updates until remediation.
5) Renewal: exceptions may be renewed, but renewal requires updated justification and evidence of progress.
- Example compensating controls: additional logging, restricted network ACLs, synthetic tests, or reduced feature scope to limit exposure.
common_risks_and_mitigations:
- Long-lived credentials: mitigation = rotate immediately, introduce short-lived tokens and scan repos for secrets.
- External backup storage outside customer region: mitigation = encrypt with customer-managed key and document transfer approvals.
- Partial audit coverage in legacy services: mitigation = wrap legacy service with a logging proxy and backlog replay for missing windows.
operational_checklists_and_playbooks:
- Quarterly: access review, key rotation, retention spot-checks, evidence pipeline dry-run.
- Pre-audit: run Evidence Pipeline -> generate package -> schedule evidence review meeting with auditor.
- Post-incident: update Evidence Vault with incident artifacts and update relevant policy documents.
